description: Hand-reviewed decisions for canonical_threat_actors.json. scripts/build_canonical_threat_actors.py applies them after the galaxy rules, so a rebuild never drops them: 'never_merge' with an 'actor' first takes the names away from that actor and never gives them back to it; 'merge' makes each name a synonym of the actor with the canonical key 'into' (an actor without an ATT&CK id that a name is the key of is folded into it; a key that no actor has yet creates the actor); 'never_merge' without an 'actor' takes each name out of every actor and lists it under 'ambiguous'; 'canonical_name' sets the display name of the actor with the key 'key' (a name with another key re-keys the actor and keeps the old key as a synonym); 'not_actor' lists names a review found to be no threat actor (a technique, malware, a kit, a hosting network, a forum, a company or a campaign that a report gave as its adversary), which the builder copies into the reference's 'not_actors' and the OTX collector drops from a pulse's adversary field; a listed name is no actor key, synonym or ambiguous name, no name another decision names, and a name the actor-name hygiene keeps as it is. Where two graph nodes are spelling variants of one name, the canonical is the node with more relationships, so that fewer edges move, unless it is an ATT&CK group's name. Each decision states its reason, date and status: 'proposed' until reviewed, then 'accepted'. Both are applied.

merge.reason: MITRE uses Lazarus Group (G0032) as an umbrella name, and the bare name is used the same way. On the graph the two nodes share seven malware families (BeaverTail, BLINDINGCAN, FudModule, InvisibleFerret, LightlessCan, Manuscrypt, ThreatNeedle); the galaxy also lists Lazarus as a synonym of this group.
Short form of the ATT&CK name of G0034; the threat-actor and ICS galaxies name this group Sandworm. On the graph the two nodes share Cyclops Blink, Industroyer2 and Prestige.
Short form of the ATT&CK name of G0047, also a galaxy synonym of this group. On the graph the two nodes share GammaLoad, GammaSteel and Pteranodon.

The ATT&CK name of G0138 with ' group' appended. The node's report describes Andariel's SmallTiger and ModeLoader campaign; no malware is shared with the ATT&CK node, whose links come from ATT&CK only.

Kept: Lotus Panda is a widely used name of Lotus Blossom (G0030). The threat-actor galaxy links its Lotus Panda record to G0030, and on the graph the two nodes share Chrysalis, Cobalt Strike and Sagerunex (46 and 64 relationships).
Name variant of the Interlock ransomware gang (an OTX-only actor, not in the galaxy). Both nodes carry the Interlock ransomware family and both reports describe the gang.
Name variant of the Beast ransomware-as-a-service gang (an OTX-only actor). Both nodes carry the Monster family, Beast's predecessor, and both reports describe the gang.

Name variant of the Fog ransomware gang (an OTX-only actor). Both nodes carry the Fog ransomware family; the group node's report is about a Fog affiliate's tooling. The bare word 'fog' is too common to be the key.

The same distinctive name with the descriptor 'APT' (an OTX-only actor). Both reports describe the ForumTroll group's targeted attacks on organisations in Russia, one the original operation and one a later phishing campaign. No malware or pulse is shared, and no other actor uses the name.

Silver Fox is its own canonical actor (see the never_merge with Void Arachne). 'silver fox apt' (29 relationships) adds the descriptor 'APT', 'silverfox' (69) drops the space; 'silver fox' (25) shares ValleyRAT with both and ABCDoor and RustSL with 'silverfox'. 'silverfox' holds the most relationships, but the canonical keeps the name as written in the galaxy and the reports.

Spacing variant of the ATT&CK name of G0082. The threat-actor galaxy files APT38 under Lazarus Group, so without this decision 'apt 38' would be a Lazarus Group synonym, while ATT&CK keeps APT38 a group of its own (the bare 'apt38' already stays with G0082).
Konni with ' group' appended; the galaxy lists Konni as a synonym of Opal Sleet, and the node shares EndRAT, RemcosRAT and RftRAT with the 'opal sleet' node.
Spelling variant of the Black Basta ransomware gang (OTX-only). 'black basta' holds 42 relationships, 'blackbasta' 41; they share the Black Basta, Cobalt Strike, DarkGate and SystemBC families.
Spelling variant of the Clop ransomware gang (OTX-only). 'clop' holds 93 relationships, 'cl0p' 68; both reports describe the gang's file-transfer exploitation campaigns and they share LemurLoot.
Spelling variant of the Dire Wolf ransomware gang that emerged in May 2025 (OTX-only). 'direwolf' holds 18 relationships, 'dire wolf' 10; both carry the Dire Wolf ransomware family.

Spelling variant of ATT&CK's Transparent Tribe (G0134; 62 relationships against 24). The node's report describes a Pakistan-nexus espionage campaign against Indian military targets, which is Transparent Tribe's.
Spelling variant of ATT&CK's TeamPCP (G1056; 151 relationships against 3). Both report supply-chain attacks on package registries, and they share router_runtime.js.
Spelling variant of ATT&CK's CyberAv3ngers (G1027; 61 relationships against 25); the galaxy's 'Cyber Av3ngers' record joins the ATT&CK group by its spacing, and the two nodes share IOCONTROL.

Spelling variant of Blind Eagle, which the galaxy lists as a synonym of APT-C-36 (G0099). On the graph of 2026-10-16 the 'blindeagle' node (38 relationships) shares Caminho, DCRat and Remcos RAT with the ATT&CK node.

ATT&CK lists Callisto Group as an alias of Star Blizzard (G1033); the galaxy keeps Callisto as a cluster of its own, whose synonyms (TAG-53, UNC4057, Blue Callisto) name the same COLDRIVER activity. On the graph of 2026-10-16 the 'callisto' node carries LOSTKEYS, NOROBOT, YESROBOT, MAYBEROBOT and COLDCOPY, which public reporting attributes to COLDRIVER / Star Blizzard.

A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary. The ransomware galaxy says Conti was developed by the TrickBot group, the threat-actor galaxy describes Wizard Spider as the operator of the TrickBot malware, malpedia says Conti is thought to be led by the group known as Wizard Spider, and ATT&CK records that Wizard Spider (G0102) uses Conti (S0575); the reference already holds GOLD ULRICK, a name for Conti's operators, as a synonym of Wizard Spider. The name therefore counts as Wizard Spider, and the actor alias merge folds an OTX actor node 'Conti' into the Wizard Spider node. The reference keeps Storm-0230 ('Conti Team 1', whose record lists WIZARD SPIDER as a synonym) as an actor of its own, so 'Conti Team 1' does not resolve to Wizard Spider. On the graph of 2026-10-17 the node (27 relationships) carries Conti, Ryuk and TrickBot.

A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary. The threat-actor galaxy records that BITWISE SPIDER uses LockBit (estimated as likely) and that BITWISE SPIDER's leak site has posted the most victims each month since July 2021 through LockBit 2.0; the other actors the galaxies link to LockBit deploy or use it, and no galaxy names another developer or operator. The name therefore counts as BITWISE SPIDER; the actor alias merge folds an OTX actor node 'LockBit' into a BITWISE SPIDER node when the graph holds one, and otherwise the node keeps its name. On the graph of 2026-10-17 the node had 71 relationships.

A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary. The threat-actor galaxy describes GOLD MANSARD as the group that operated the Nemty ransomware, whose operator retired Nemty in April 2020, after which Nefilim was introduced without an affiliate model; the ransomware galaxy relates Nefilim to Nemty and lists Nefilim among the later names of JSWorm, the family that became Nemty. The threat-actor galaxy names TRAVELING SPIDER, an actor the reference holds, as the developer of Nemty; it does not name Nefilim. The name therefore counts as GOLD MANSARD; the actor alias merge folds an OTX actor node 'Nefilim' into a GOLD MANSARD node when the graph holds one, and otherwise the node keeps its name. On the graph of 2026-10-17 the node had 14 relationships.

Spelling variant of SAMBASPIDER, which the threat-actor galaxy lists as the actor associated with the Mispadu banking trojan. The OTX report on the graph's 'samba spider' node names the adversary 'SAMBA SPIDER' and reviews the Latin American banking malware of 2024, Mispadu among it. No galaxy gives either spelling to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 28 relationships, among them Mispadu; the graph holds no 'sambaspider' node.

Spelling variant of Markopolo, which the threat-actor galaxy describes as an actor that runs scams against cryptocurrency users through a fake application, Vortax, and uses social media to make them look legitimate. The OTX report on the graph's 'marko polo' node names the adversary 'Marko Polo', a cybercriminal group that runs scams through social media, impersonating brands of virtual-meeting and cryptocurrency software, with Stealc, Rhadamanthys and HijackLoader. No galaxy gives either spelling to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 16 relationships; the graph holds no 'markopolo' node.

Spelling variant of TA558, which the threat-actor galaxy describes as a financially motivated actor that sends malicious e-mails with business-themed lures to distribute at least 15 different malware payloads. The OTX report on the graph's 'ta-558' node names the adversary 'TA-558' for a spearphishing campaign that delivers Snake Keylogger. No galaxy gives either spelling to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 10 relationships; the graph holds no 'ta558' node.

Spelling variant of 'isoon', which the microsoft-activity-group and threat-actor galaxies list as a synonym of Houndstooth Typhoon. The OTX report on the graph's 'i-soon' node names the adversary 'I-SOON', the Chinese contractor whose leaked documents tie it to several state-sponsored groups. No galaxy gives the name to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 11 relationships, ten of them techniques, and no malware; the graph holds no 'houndstooth typhoon' node.

APT-C-13 is the 360net-threat-actor galaxy's designation of Sandworm. Its record, the Chinese name of Sandworm with the designation (synonym SandWorm), is the only galaxy record that carries the designation, and the galaxy relates it to the threat-actor galaxy's Sandworm record and the microsoft-activity-group galaxy's Seashell Blizzard record, both joined to Sandworm Team (G0034). The build leaves the record out because its name without the designation joins no ATT&CK actor. Both OTX reports on the graph's 'apt-c-13' node state that APT-C-13 (Sandworm) is also known as FROZENBARENTS, an ATT&CK alias of G0034, and one names the adversary 'APT-C-13, Sandworm, FROZENBARENTS'. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 28 relationships, 26 of them techniques, and no malware.

APT-C-53 is the 360net-threat-actor galaxy's designation of Gamaredon. Its record 'Gamaredon - APT-C-53' is the only galaxy record that carries the designation. It describes a Russian state-sponsored group, active since at least 2013, that targets Ukrainian government, defence, diplomatic and media organisations, and it names Primitive Bear, Winterflounder and BlueAlpha, which the reference holds as synonyms of Gamaredon Group (G0047). The build leaves the record out because its name without the designation joins no ATT&CK actor. Both OTX reports on the graph's 'apt-c-53' node name the adversary 'APT-C-53 (Gamaredon)': one states that APT-C-53 is also known as Gamaredon, the other that it is also known as Primitive Bear, Winterflounder and BlueAlpha. No galaxy gives the designation to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 22 relationships, 21 of them techniques, and no malware.

APT-C-55 is the 360net-threat-actor galaxy's designation of Kimsuky. Its record 'Kimsuky - APT-C-55' is the only galaxy record that carries the designation. It describes a North Korean group, first reported in 2013, that targets South Korean think tanks and government, diplomatic, media and academic organisations. The build joins the record to Kimsuky (G0094), whose synonyms include 'kimsuky - apt-c-55'. The OTX report on the graph's 'apt-c-55' node names the adversary 'APT-C-55 (Kimsuky)'. It describes a campaign against South Korea with the HappyDoor backdoor whose scripts, backdoor families and domain naming match Kimsuky's earlier activity. No galaxy gives the designation to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node (19 relationships, one OTX report) carries HappyDoor, which another OTX report attributes to the Kimsuky node.

An OTX report names the adversary 'TA4557/FIN6', which the actor-name hygiene keeps as one name because it does not split on '/'. The report covers an intrusion that began with a resume lure and used More_eggs, Cobalt Strike, Pyramid C2 and Cloudflared. Both parts of the name belong to FIN6 (G0037): FIN6 is its ATT&CK name, and the threat-actor galaxy lists TA4557 among FIN6's synonyms (the reference holds 'ta4557' as a synonym of FIN6). No galaxy gives either name to another actor. The three OTX reports on the FIN6 node describe the same activity: two report resume and job-seeker lures delivering More_eggs, one reports Pyramid C2 servers, and all three list More_eggs, Terra Loader, SKID and SpicyOmelette. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the 'ta4557/fin6' node (32 relationships, one OTX report) shares More_eggs and Terra Loader with the FIN6 node.

Replaces the merge of 'agenda' into an actor 'qilin' of 2026-10-17. A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: OTX reports name Qilin and Agenda as the adversary. ATT&CK describes Water Galura (G1050) as the operators of the Qilin Ransomware-as-a-Service, who handle payload generation, ransom negotiations and the publication of stolen data. ATT&CK also lists Agenda as an alias of Qilin (S1242), and malpedia records that Qilin was first observed in July 2022 under the name Agenda, so Agenda is Qilin's earlier name. ATT&CK and malpedia describe Qilin as run with affiliates. The only other group ATT&CK links to it, Moonstone Sleet (G1036), uses it, and no galaxy names another developer or operator. The names therefore count as Water Galura, and the actor alias merge folds OTX actor nodes 'Qilin' and 'Agenda' into the Water Galura node. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the 'qilin' node (84 relationships, eight OTX reports, 'agenda' already folded into it) carries the Qilin and Agenda families, and the Water Galura node uses Qilin.

KongTuke is a name of TAG-124. The malpedia galaxy's KongTuke record (399a788c-0487-403d-903e-715afe56b9f0) describes a traffic distribution system, discovered around May 2024, that redirects visitors of compromised CMS websites through fake update lures and, from the beginning of 2025, fake CAPTCHA lures, and that is likely an initial access service selling infections to ransomware affiliates and other access vendors; it lists TAG-124 and js.LandUpdate808 as synonyms. The threat-actor galaxy's TAG-124 record (8a1b831c-e07e-43ad-933a-7fe7a9a1e449) describes the same activity, a traffic distribution system that injects JavaScript into WordPress sites, leads victims to fake browser update pages, distributes MintsLoader and uses the ClickFix technique, and lists LandUpdate808 as its synonym. No galaxy gives the name to another actor. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the OTX actor node 'kongtuke' (5 relationships, one OTX report) carries CrashFix, ModeloRAT and NexShield, and the 'tag-124' node (49 relationships, three OTX reports) carries MintsLoader; the two nodes share no family, and ModeloRAT is also listed in one of the TAG-124 reports, which names five actors. A Malware node 'kongtuke' comes from two other OTX reports, which name no actor on the graph. The name therefore counts as TAG-124: the actor alias merge folds the 'kongtuke' node into the 'tag-124' node, and an OTX report that names KongTuke both as its adversary and as a malware family keeps it as an actor, which counts as TAG-124.

An OTX report names the adversary 'INC', the name of the operation's ransomware. ATT&CK describes INC Ransom (G1032) as a ransomware and data extortion threat group associated with the deployment of INC Ransomware since at least July 2023, most often against the industrial, healthcare and education sectors in the US and Europe, and INC Ransomware (S1139) as a strain used by the INC Ransom group; malpedia lists the family as 'INC', and the ransomware galaxy lists the operation's leak sites under 'inc ransom'. The threat-actor galaxy describes Storm-0494's intrusions, exploited by groups such as Vice Society, deploying the INC ransomware payload, which makes them deployers rather than the operator, and malpedia records that Lynx bought INC ransomware source code; no galaxy names another developer or operator. The name therefore counts as INC Ransom, and the actor alias merge folds the OTX node 'INC' into the INC Ransom node. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the 'inc' node (36 relationships, two OTX reports, healthcare, United States) carries Lynx, Sinobi, Brave Prince and Cobalt Strike; the INC Ransom node (75 relationships) carries INC Ransomware.

ATT&CK's campaign 2025 Poland Wiper Attacks (C0063) records that some reporting assessed the activity as consistent with the Russian Federal Security Service group Dragonfly (G0035), 'also tracked as STATIC TUNDRA', while other reporting attributes the destructive wiper activity to Sandworm Team (G0034). The campaign text thus gives Static Tundra as another name of Dragonfly; no galaxy gives the name to another actor, and no ATT&CK alias or galaxy synonym holds it. Three OTX reports name the adversary 'Static Tundra': one covers the DynoWiper and LazyWiper attacks with Impacket and Rubeus, software ATT&CK lists for C0063, and two list PS1Bot and XenoRAT. The decision rests on the name alone: the actor alias merge folds the OTX node 'Static Tundra' with its links into the Dragonfly node, so the reports' attributions, the contested wiper campaign included, then stand on Dragonfly. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the node has 36 relationships (energy; Poland the most targeted country on its indicators) and shares DynoWiper with the Sandworm Team node; the Dragonfly node (87 relationships) shares no family with it.

The threat-actor galaxy's Storm-0473 record names the actor 'Storm-0473 (Tomiris)' and describes a group active since at least 2019 that primarily targets government and diplomatic entities in the Commonwealth of Independent States with downloaders, backdoors and file stealers written in different programming languages; it notes potential ties to Turla but treats the two as separate actors. The reference holds Storm-0473, with the synonym UNC2849, from this record, and no galaxy gives the name Tomiris to another actor. ATT&CK (S0671) and malpedia also name a Go backdoor Tomiris; the reference already holds such shared names as synonyms (Havex for Dragonfly, KeyBoy for Tropic Trooper). The OTX report on the graph's 'tomiris' node names the adversary 'Tomiris' and lists twelve 'Tomiris' implants (reverse shells and reverse SOCKS proxies, a downloader, a file grabber and a Telegram backdoor) written in C#, C++, Go, Python, Rust and PowerShell, with Distopia, JLORAT, Havoc and AdaptixC2; malpedia's only report reference for JLORAT is a report on Tomiris. The report's indicators target Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the node has 35 relationships; the graph holds no 'storm-0473' node.

LapDogs is the operational relay box (ORB) network that the threat-actor galaxy's UAT-7810 record describes UAT-7810 as maintaining. The same record names UAT-7810 as the developer of the SHORTLEASH, LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH and JARLEASH backdoors and adds that it provides infrastructure to secondary APTs. Malpedia's ShortLeash records describe ShortLeash as a custom backdoor used to create an ORB network and cite the LapDogs report. An OTX report names the adversary 'LapDogs' with the ShortLeash family, and no galaxy gives the name to another actor. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the 'lapdogs' node (21 relationships, OTX only) carries ShortLeash, which the 'uat-7810' node (27 relationships) carries together with LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH, JARLEASH and LEASHTEST.

APT-C-01 is the 360net-threat-actor galaxy's designation of the group it names 毒云藤 ('poison cloud vine'). Its record '毒云藤 - APT-C-01' is the only galaxy record that carries the designation. It describes a group, active since at least 2007, that has conducted espionage against defence, government, science and technology, education and maritime organisations in China, gives Taiwan as its country and lists 绿斑 ('green spot') among its synonyms. The threat-actor galaxy's GreenSpot record, which the reference holds as the actor GreenSpot, describes a group believed to operate from Taiwan, active since at least 2007, that targets government, academic and military entities in China; it lists PoisonVine (the English form of the 360net name) and APT-Q-20 as synonyms and cites a 2019 conference paper on a long-term 'vine' attack against China. The build leaves the 360net record out because its name without the designation joins no ATT&CK actor. No galaxy gives the designation to another actor. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the 'apt-c-01' node (19 relationships, one OTX report on defence, government, technology and education targets) carries Sliver RAT, and the 'greenspot' node (11 relationships, one OTX report on government, education and defence targets) carries no malware; the actor alias merge folds the 'apt-c-01' node into it.

The threat-actor galaxy's name Calypso with ' APT' appended. The galaxy's Calypso record (synonyms BRONZE MEDLEY and Red Lamassu), which the reference holds as the actor Calypso, describes a group active since at least September 2016 that steals confidential data from government agencies in Brazil, India, Kazakhstan, Russia, Thailand and Turkey; one of its references is the 2019 report on the group filed as 'calypso-apt-2019'. No galaxy gives the name to another actor. The OTX report on the graph's 'calypso apt' node names it together with Rocke, Threat Group-3390 and Cloud Snooper and lists Noodle RAT, Gh0st RAT, Rekoobe and seven other families; as a report that names several actors it attributes its malware to none of them, and the merge only lets the name count as Calypso. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the node has 19 relationships, 18 of them techniques, and no malware; the graph holds no 'calypso' node.

Short form of 'Donot Team', which the threat-actor galaxy lists as a synonym of VICEROY TIGER together with APT-C-35. The 360net-threat-actor galaxy's record '肚脑虫 - APT-C-35' lists Donot as its synonym and describes APT-C-35 as a group also called Donot that conducts cyber-espionage against government bodies of the countries around the Kashmir region; the build leaves that record out because it joins no ATT&CK actor. Malpedia's 'DONOT' is a malware toolkit and 'Unidentified 117 (Donot Loader)' a loader; no galaxy gives the name to another actor. Two OTX reports name the adversary DONOT; on the graph of 2026-11-03 the 'donot' node has 13 relationships, among them the Tanzeem family, and the graph holds no 'viceroy tiger' node.

Spelling variant of UNG0002 with one zero dropped; no galaxy lists a group UNG002. The threat-actor galaxy's UNG0002 record (3a24ac96-4ae4-456f-bacd-29259a21935f) describes an espionage group that targets China, Hong Kong and Pakistan with LNK and VBScript lures and tools such as Cobalt Strike and Metasploit. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the OTX actor node 'ung002' (3 relationships, one OTX report of 2026-05-20) carries Cobalt Strike, and the report's indicators name China as the targeted country; the 'ung0002' node (24 relationships, one OTX report of 2025-07-16) carries the group's techniques. The name therefore counts as UNG0002, and the actor alias merge folds the 'ung002' node into the 'ung0002' node.

The threat-actor galaxy's UTA0178 record (f288f686-b5b3-4c86-9960-5f8fb18709a3) lists ARMORY CASTLE among its synonyms, together with UNC5221 and Red Dev 61, in the public misp-galaxy release v359 of the threat-actor galaxy, and adds a report on ARMORY CASTLE's exploitation activity to its references. The MISP galaxies captured on 2026-11-05 carry the record at v352, with UNC5221 and Red Dev 61 only, so the build does not take the name yet. The reference holds UTA0178, with the synonym UNC5221, from this record, and no record of the galaxies captured on 2026-11-05 or of the v359 threat-actor galaxy gives the name to another actor. Two OTX reports (2026-10-16 and 2026-10-20) name the adversary 'ARMORY CASTLE' with the SAWFLY and BARECLAW families, which no galaxy describes. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the 'armory castle' node (35 relationships, 31 of them techniques) carries SAWFLY and BARECLAW, which no other actor carries, and shares no malware with the 'uta0178' node (73 relationships, six OTX reports); the decision rests on the galaxy synonym. Once the MISP galaxies are at v359 or later, the galaxy gives the name and the decision only confirms it.

The threat-actor galaxy's UNC5820 record (e13e36e7-a75b-42fa-8d51-35f9eeafebfc) lists CL-STA-0954 as its synonym in the public misp-galaxy release v359 of the threat-actor galaxy. The MISP galaxies captured on 2026-11-05 carry the record at v352, without synonyms, so the build does not take the name yet. The record describes an actor that exploits CVE-2024-47575 to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands, and that exfiltrated configuration data, user information and hashed passwords of the managed devices; v359 adds to its references a report on the exploitation of CVE-2024-47575 with the PeerStitch malware. No record of the galaxies captured on 2026-11-05 or of the v359 threat-actor galaxy gives the name to another actor; CL-STA-0969, a synonym of Pepper Typhoon in the microsoft-activity-group galaxy, is another designation. An OTX report of 2026-10-14 names the adversary 'CL-STA-0954' with the PeerStitch family. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the 'cl-sta-0954' node (23 relationships, 20 of them techniques) carries PeerStitch with eleven indicators, and no other actor carries it; the 'unc5820' node (21 relationships, two OTX reports of October 2024) shares no malware with it. Once the MISP galaxies are at v359 or later, the galaxy gives the name and the decision only confirms it.

never_merge.reason: Not merged: the threat-actor galaxy lists Silver Fox as a synonym of Void Arachne, a vendor equivalence that is not universally accepted (the two share ValleyRAT and Winos 4.0, families several Chinese-speaking clusters use). A wrong merge is worse than a missed one.

Not merged: the threat-actor galaxy lists Famous Chollima as a synonym of Wagemole, a vendor equivalence that is not universally accepted (both name overlapping North Korean IT-worker and fake-interview activity). A wrong merge is worse than a missed one.

Not merged: the threat-actor galaxy lists TA488 as a synonym of Void Blizzard, a vendor equivalence that is not universally accepted; the two graph nodes share no malware or pulse. A wrong merge is worse than a missed one.

Doubtful: the node's only malware link is 'green lambert - s0690', an unrelated ATT&CK malware family that looks like a bad extraction (the name appears inside 'Lambert'); merging would carry that link to the gang. Its report and that of 'bert ransomware' describe the same gang, so revisit once the extraction is fixed.

Doubtful: the node's only report is a monthly vulnerability-prioritisation digest, not an Interlock report, and none of its malware links (GhostBlade, GhostKnife, GhostSaber, PlasmaGrid, PlasmaLoader) is shared with the other Interlock nodes; merging would attach them to the gang.

A malware family name, not a group. A galaxy lists it as a synonym of Storm-2460, but an actor node named after the stealer gathers reports on its many distributors; merging would attribute all of them to one group.

Common words that only the suffix rule derives, from 'Comment Group' (APT1), 'Tsar Team' (APT28), 'Beijing Group' (Elderwood), 'Iron Group' and 'Hacking Team'. As bare names they do not identify one actor.

Doubtful short forms the suffix rule derives from 'Tonto Team' (G0131) and 'Pacha Group': both are common words (Spanish 'tonto', and a title and brand name), and the reports name the groups in full. Neither is a graph name today. The other short forms checked (gorgon, sunshop, chronus, belsen, daixin) are distinctive and kept.

A malware family name. ATT&CK lists 'BlackEnergy (Group)' as an alias of Sandworm Team (G0034); EdgeGuard's actor-name hygiene drops the parenthetical, which leaves the malware's name, so the bare name is not taken as the group ('blackenergy group' still is).

Bare names that only the suffix rule derives, from 'Poseidon Group' (G0033) and 'Shamoon Group'; both are also malware family names (the Poseidon stealer, the Shamoon wiper used by several groups), so the bare name does not identify one actor.

Not merged: the threat-actor galaxy's record 'Cold River' (synonyms Nahr Elbard and Nahr el bared) has one reference, a report on the Agent_Drable implant, which malpedia lists as a synonym of the DNSpionage malware. The record describes an actor that uses DNS subdomain hijacking, certificate spoofing and tunnelled command-and-control traffic, and it has no galaxy relation to Star Blizzard (G1033) or to the threat-actor galaxy's Callisto record. The build joins it to Star Blizzard only because 'Cold River' is a spacing variant of COLDRIVER, an ATT&CK alias of G1033. No Star Blizzard or Callisto record in any galaxy lists the three names. The names are kept away from Star Blizzard and resolve to no actor. The decision takes the names, not the join: the record stays listed among Star Blizzard's records and gives it none of its names. COLDRIVER and COLD RELIC, which the Callisto record lists, stay synonyms of Star Blizzard. No OTX report on the graph or in MISP of 2026-10-22 names any of the three.

Not merged: 'fire ant' differs only by a space from FIREANT, an ATT&CK alias of Mustang Panda (G0129), but the galaxies give that spelling to two different actors: ATT&CK to Mustang Panda, and the microsoft-activity-group galaxy, as 'FireAnt', to Pink Sandstorm (Agrius, G1030). The name therefore does not identify one actor by its spelling. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the 'fire ant' node (21 relationships, OTX only) has no malware, only techniques, and its only OTX report also names Salt Typhoon. The name is kept away from Mustang Panda and counts as itself. A wrong merge is worse than a missed one.

Not merged: an OTX adversary string that joins two names with ' - ', which the actor-name hygiene keeps as one name. Its parts are two actors the reference holds apart: Scattered Lapsus Hunters, from the threat-actor galaxy's record 'Scattered Lapsus Hunters' (c216b83d-f298-438c-be47-0506ec773d8f, v352, synonym Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters), which describes an alliance of Scattered Spider, LAPSUS$ and ShinyHunters, and ShinyHunters (G1057; mitre-intrusion-set 'ShinyHunters - G1057', 5e30362d-935b-4b1c-8bf2-96c7b7b7e299, v44), whose description gives Scattered Lapsus Hunters as one of the names public reporting uses for operations of ShinyHunters members with members of other groups, not as an alias. A list of names is not a synonym, and a merge into either actor would drop the other. The name is listed as ambiguous and counts as itself. On the graph of 2026-11-03 its node has 5 relationships (four techniques and the source, no malware) from one OTX report of 2025-09-10. A wrong merge is worse than a missed one.

not_actor.reason: A social-engineering technique, not a group: a fake CAPTCHA or 'fix' prompt that makes the user paste and run a command. The galaxies describe many actors as using it: the threat-actor galaxy's GrayBravo 'employs the ClickFix technique to distribute malware', Hive0163 uses 'ClickFix social engineering for initial access', and TAG-124, UAC-0227, TAG-140 and GrayCharlie are described the same way; malpedia's IClickFix uses 'the ClickFix social engineering tactic'. No galaxy has an actor record named ClickFix. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor node 'clickfix' (38 relationships, three OTX reports) carries CrashFix, ModeloRAT, CastleLoader, CastleStealer, Lumma Stealer, NetSupport RAT and SectopRAT, payloads of several actors, and eleven other OTX reports list ClickFix as a malware family.

Self-propagating supply-chain worms, not groups. ATT&CK lists Shai-Hulud (S9008) as a supply chain worm first reported in September 2025, Mini Shai-Hulud (S9043) as a credential stealer and self-replicating supply chain worm derived from Shai-Hulud that TeamPCP (G1056) has used, and GlassWorm (S9010) as a worm that propagated through supply chain attacks by compromising repository credentials; malpedia lists Shai-Hulud and GlassWorm as malware families. No galaxy has an actor record of these names. OTX reports give the worms as their adversary: on the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor nodes 'shai-hulud' (35 relationships, four OTX reports, four of its five families also on the TeamPCP node), 'mini shai-hulud' (16) and 'glassworm' (29) stand beside the Malware nodes of the same names, which come from ATT&CK and OTX.

Information stealers available to many actors, not groups. ATT&CK lists Agent Tesla (S0331) as a spyware Trojan written for the .NET framework, and malpedia as a .NET information stealer readily available to actors due to leaked builders. ATT&CK lists Lumma Stealer (S1213) as malware-as-a-service; the reference marks 'lumma stealer' never_merge because an actor node named after the stealer gathers the reports on its many distributors, and the bare 'lumma' is the same case. No galaxy has an actor record of either name. The OTX report on 'agent tesla' gives it as the adversary without listing a malware family, so the rule for an adversary the same report lists as a family does not apply; the report on 'lumma' pairs it with Lumma Stealer. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor nodes have 10 and 15 relationships, beside the Malware nodes 'agent tesla' (ATT&CK and eight OTX reports) and 'lumma' (15 OTX reports).

macOS information stealers, not groups. Malpedia lists AMOS with the synonym Atomic macOS Stealer, whose references describe the stealer sold on Telegram, and BANSHEE (osx.banshee), a macOS stealer whose source code leaked. No galaxy has an actor record named AMOS or Banshee; Black Banshee, a synonym the reference gives to Kimsuky, and Void Banshee, an actor of its own, are other actors. On the graph of 2026-11-03 'amos' (10 relationships) and 'amos threat group' (21 relationships, the stealer's name with 'threat group' appended) come from OTX reports that list no malware family, while eight OTX Malware nodes carry the stealer under its names (amos, atomic macos stealer, atomic stealer and others). The report on 'banshee' (26 relationships) lists Banshee Stealer and Lumma Stealer as its families; the adversary differs from the family by the type word, so the rule for an adversary the same report lists as a family does not catch it.

Information stealers, not groups. Malpedia and the stealer galaxy list DarkCloud Stealer, a stealer written in Visual Basic. Malpedia lists TamperedChef (win.tampered_chef) as a malware family, with references titled 'tamperedchef-the-bad-pdf-editor' and 'hunting-for-tamperedchef-infostealer', and its BaoLoader record tells BaoLoader apart from TamperedChef. No galaxy has an actor record of either name. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor nodes 'darkcloud' (15 relationships, techniques only) and 'tamperedchef' (31 relationships, three OTX reports, attributed the two families one of them lists, 'calendaromatic' and 'imagelooker', which no galaxy records) stand beside the Malware nodes 'darkcloud', 'darkcloud stealer' and 'tamperedchef' of other OTX reports.

Botnets, not groups. ATT&CK lists ANDROMEDA (S1074) as commodity malware, and the botnet galaxy describes the Andromeda botnet, also known as Gamarue or Wauchos, as used to distribute large quantities of malware; the threat-actor galaxy's ANDROMEDA SPIDER is another name, which the reference holds as an actor of its own. The botnet galaxy's BadBox record and malpedia's BADBOX describe a cybercriminal operation selling Android devices with preinstalled malware; 'BADBOX 2.0' is that name with a version, and its OTX report pairs it with the BADBOX family. The botnet galaxy describes Prometei as a cryptocurrency-mining botnet, and malpedia lists its Windows and ELF variants. No galaxy has an actor record of these names. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor node 'andromeda/gamarue' (17 relationships) is attributed the ATT&CK Malware node 'andromeda', 'badbox 2.0' (12) is the only actor the Malware node 'badbox' is attributed to, and 'prometei' (19, techniques only) stands beside a Malware node of four other OTX reports.

Botnets of routers and IoT devices, not groups. Malpedia describes PolarEdge as a TLS backdoor on Cisco, Asus, QNAP and Synology devices, possibly used as operational relay boxes, and cites a report on an IoT botnet. RondoDox has no galaxy record; on the graph it is a Malware node of eleven OTX reports, often with other botnet and miner families (Kinsing, Mirai, XMRig). No galaxy has an actor record of either name. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor nodes 'polaredge' and 'rondodox' (14 relationships each, techniques only) come from OTX reports that list no malware family, beside the Malware nodes of the same names.

Malware that the galaxies give to an operator and that several actors use, not groups. ATT&CK lists SocGholish (S1124) as JavaScript-based loader malware operated by Mustard Tempest (G1020); malpedia lists it under FAKEUPDATES, and the tool galaxy uses the name for both the drive-by download network and the loader. The banker galaxy describes DanaBot as a Trojan with banking web injections and stealer functions, and the threat-actor galaxy mentions SCULLY SPIDER as its operator. Neither is merged into its operator: on the graph of 2026-11-03 the Malware node 'socgholish' is attributed to Mustard Tempest, RansomHub, Water Scylla, UNC4108 and RomCom, and 'danabot' to Storm-1865 and Mustard Tempest, so a synonym of one operator would give the other actors' reports to it. The actor nodes 'socgholish' (8 relationships) and 'danabot' (2) come from one OTX report each.

Malware, not groups. Malpedia lists Cloud Snooper (elf.cloud_snooper, synonym Snoopy) as a Linux (ELF) malware family, whose references are reports on Cloud Snooper and overviews of Linux threats; no actor galaxy has the name. Squidoor and Batavia have no galaxy record; on the graph each is a Malware node of another OTX report, Squidoor attributed to REF7707 (the threat-actor galaxy's REF7707, synonyms CL-STA-0049 and Jewelbug), and another report gives Batavia both as its adversary and as its malware family. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor nodes carry techniques only: 'cloud snooper' (19 relationships) because its one OTX report names it beside Calypso APT, Rocke and Threat Group-3390, so the report's ten families were attributed to none of them, and 'squidoor' (8) and 'batavia' (17) because their OTX reports list no malware family. Their techniques are those of a backdoor (server software component, exfiltration over the C2 channel) or of spyware (screen capture, data from the local system).

Tools offered to many customers, not groups. Malpedia describes GhostSocks as a Golang-based proxy malware first advertised as malware-as-a-service; on the graph its Malware node is attributed to Storm-3075 and Water Kurita. Darcula is a phishing kit: the threat-actor galaxy's XinXin record says that XinXin also develops and uses other phishing kits like Lighthouse and Darcula, and the graph holds a Malware node 'darcula' from an OTX report on phishing kits. Shanya has no galaxy record; the OTX report on it attributes to it ten families of unrelated operations, among them the Qilin, Medusa and Akira ransomware, which the reference gives to three different actors, and its seven techniques are those of a packer or crypter (DLL side-loading, rundll32, obfuscation, process injection, disabling security tools). As for 'lumma stealer' (never_merge), an actor node named after a product gathers the reports on its many users. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor nodes have 8, 13 and 19 relationships.

Malware or toolset names, not groups; the evidence is the name form and the graph. 'GrelosGTM' is malpedia's Grelos, 'a skimmer used for magecart-style attacks', with 'GTM' appended; its OTX report pairs it only with the generic family 'JavaScript sniffer' on five domains. 'GroozaV2' is the report's own family Grooza with a version suffix: all 242 indicators of the report carry the pair Grooza::GroozaV2, and the Malware node 'grooza' comes from this report only. 'PCPJack' is a malware family of another OTX report (container, SSH and cron techniques); the report that gives it as the adversary attributes to it only the public tools Chisel and Sliver. No galaxy has an actor record of these names. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the actor nodes have 21, 13 and 16 relationships.

Network infrastructure, not groups. Proton66 is a bulletproof hosting network: twelve malpedia records cite the report 'PROSPERO & Proton66: Uncovering the links between bulletproof networks' or a report filed as 'proton66-part-2-compromised-wordpress-pages-and-malware-campaigns', on campaigns its address space hosted. IPIDEA has no galaxy record; the OTX report that gives it as the adversary attributes to it Kimwolf (malpedia: Android malware that 'uses compromised systems to relay malicious and abusive Internet traffic'; the botnet galaxy: a dual-purpose residential proxy and DDoS botnet), the BADBOX operation and the Mirai-derived Aisuru botnet, and its techniques include Proxy (T1090) and Compromise Infrastructure (T1584): the residential proxy network these botnets feed, not their author. No galaxy has an actor record of either name. On the graph of 2026-11-03 the node 'proton66' (34 relationships, two OTX reports) carries SuperBlack, Strela Stealer, Weaxor, Remcos and XWorm; all but Weaxor are also attributed to other actors (SuperBlack to Mora_001, Strela Stealer to Hive0145, Remcos and XWorm to more than ten each), and 'ipidea' (20) carries Kimwolf, Aisuru and BADBOX 2.0.

A cybercrime forum, not a group. The threat-actor galaxy describes it as a place where actors post and sell stolen data: its IntelBroker record names 'underground forums like BreachForums', Nam3L3ss is described as 'distributing this data on BreachForums', and the GhostR and MORH4x records name it the same way.
